newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asia Metals-S.Koreans keep shipping stocks abroad.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals-S.Koreans keep shipping stocks abroad.

text.p: South Korean metal houses have continued to ship much of their stocks overseas to cut carrying costs as demand remains low, traders said on Thursday.
They said domestic demand was low due to the continued economic slump and a seasonal summer slowdown.
They estimate South Korea's copper and copper product exports to have surged 51.9 percent to 98,755 tonnes in the first five months of this year from 65,018 tonnes a year ago.
Aluminium and aluminium product exports were estimated to have jumped 58.6 percent to 110,360 tonnes from 69,602 tonnes.
The domestic aluminium market remained depressed by concerns about more debt defaults by small- and medium-sized metal companies, the traders said.
"There seemed to be no spot deals but only some long-term contracts," a trader with Tong Yang Global said.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery remained firm at between $95-$100 a tonne CIF Pusan over London Metal Exchange cash prices, the traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices stood at around 1,540,000 won a tonne over the past week, they said.

Last week LG Metals Corp, South Korea's largest copper producer, raised its domestic price by 3.5 percent to 2,553,000 won a tonne for July from 2,467,000 won a month earlier. It is an affiliate of the LG Group.
Korea Zinc, the country's largest zinc and lead producer, also raised its monthly domestic zinc price by 2.1 percent to 1,386,000 won a tonne from 1,358,000 won in June.
But the company cut by 0.9 percent the lead price for July to 678,000 won a tonne from 684,000 won.
